docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Table 1:

DAC Module

Solution Pros Cons Option 1. MCP4921-E/P$2.81/eachlink to product - 12-bit resolution- SPI interface- Through-hole PDIP-8 package- 2.7 V to 5.5 V operation- Fast shipping speed - Requires external reference voltage- High unit price Option 2. MCP4801-E/P $1.61/each Link to product - Easier implementation - Through-hole PDIP-8 - SPI interface- Fast shipping speed - Lower waveform quality - 8-bit resolution - More quantization noise

Choice: Option 1: MCP4921-E/P DAC

Rationale: The MCP4921 was chosen because it provides 12-bit resolution. This allows the microcontroller to generate smoother and more accurate analog waveforms for the alarm/ speaker. It also uses SPI communication, which is supported by the PIC18F57Q43, which will make it easy to integrate into the system while keeping fast data transfer. The through-hole PDIP package also simplifies PCB assembly and soldering, since I would I am not the greatest at soldering.

Table 2:

Audio Amplifier Module

Solution Pros Cons Option 1. LM386N-3/NOPB audio amplifier$1.18/eachlink to product * Designed for speakers* Through-hole PDIP-8* Operates from 4–12 V * Requires capacitors* Audio quality not as good as modern Class-D amps * Option 2. LM358N audio amplifier Price not shown * Link to product - Through-hole DIP-8 - Wide power supply range - Suitable for battery operation (if as a group we decide to use that) - Not an audio amplifier - Slow shipping speed and non-refundable- no price shown on Digikey

Choice: Option 1: LM386N-3 audio amplifier

Rationale: The LM386 was chosen because it is designed for audio amplification and can directly drive an 8 Ω speaker from a 5 V supply which is very helpful since I will not need to introduce another power supply. This makes it a practical choice for increasing the output power of the DAC signal so that the alarm can be heard clearly. Lastly, the DIP package is easy to solder (I am not good at soldering) and is very commonly used in audio projects so I will be able to access resources on the part if I am having any trouble with this part during construction.

Table 3:

Speaker Module

Solution Pros Cons Option 1. ADS01008MR-LW100-R speaker$2.77/eachlink to product - Perfect for simple alarm tones and beeps- Smaller footprint (10 mm diameter)- 0.5 W rated power - Limited frequency range (1500 Hz to 6000 Hz)- Will Not very loud (82 dB SPL) Option 2. \CMS-23558N-L152 speaker $6.07/each Link to product - Wide frequency response (440 Hz to 20 kHz)- Very good sound quality - Fast shipping speed - Way More expensive - Larger Footprint/ - Requires more amplifier power

Choice: Option 2: CMS-23558N-L152 speaker

Rationale: The CMS-23558N-L152 was chosen because it can produce a louder and clearer alarm signal. As well as, support a much wider frequency range than the other speaker. The 8 Ω impedance is compatible with the LM386 amplifier, and the larger speaker size allows for improved sound quality but will result in a larger footprint, but I believe that it is a challenge I am willing to take for the better performance. The increased cost is also a con, but I believe that the pros of the speaker outweigh that con. Table 3:

Voltage Regulator Model

Solution Pros Cons Option 1. L7805CV Voltage Regulator$1.14/eachlink to product - Produces a stable 5V output- TO-220 package allows for easy mounting and soldering- Used in class so familiar with how it works and will be able to get help from teaching team if having problems - Requires 7V minimum voltage so if barrel jack is not working properly it will not work- Linear voltage regulator so excess voltage turns into heat which could damage product Option 2. \LM7805CT Volatge Regulator $1.74/each Link to product - Common industry standard regulator- Well documented and reliable - Will require a flat $14.00 shipping fee for the product - Low maximum output current of roughly 1A/ - minimum 10-day shipping

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The purpose of the power budget was to make sure all of the components in the system could be powered safely by the selected power supply and voltage regulator. To do this, the current requirements of each component were added together and a 25% safety margin was included. The results showed that the system requires about 214 mA, which is well below the 1 A capacity of the LM7805 regulator and the 9 V wall adapter, confirming that the design has enough available power to operate reliably.

docs.title: Conclusions
docs.text: The power budget shows that the system only requires about 214 mA, including a 25% safety margin, which is well below the 1 A limit of the LM7805 regulator and 9 V power supply. This means the selected power components can safely and reliably power the entire system.
